headline: SpaceXAI's Grok 4.6 matches GPT-5.6 performance and overtakes Kimi K3
summary: Grok 4.6 scores 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, tying OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol Max and improving significantly over its predecessor in coding and knowledge work.
details: SpaceXAI has launched Grok 4.6, its newest frontier AI model, focusing on long-running agents, coding, and knowledge work. The model achieves a score of 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, placing it as the world's third-best AI model.

This new version surpasses Moonshot's Kimi K3 and matches OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol Max. It shows significant improvements over Grok 4.5 High, increasing its score by five points on the index. Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 and Fable 5 remain the top two models.

Grok 4.6 demonstrates substantial gains in coding, terminal tasks, knowledge work, and agent benchmarks compared to its predecessor. It maintains a competitive API pricing starting at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens, making it a mid-priced option among leading proprietary and open-source models.

The model is now available through Grok Build, SpaceXAI's platform for AI agents, and is also integrated into Cursor, SpaceX's recently acquired AI coding startup. It is also accessible via partners like OpenRouter, Vercel, and Cloudflare.

SpaceXAI has enhanced Grok 4.6 with a longer supplemental training run, focusing on curated reasoning and technical data. The company also adjusted its optimizer and training recipe, and used Grok 4.5 to regenerate supervised fine-tuning trajectories across various domains.

The company emphasizes Grok 4.6's ability to stay on task for extended periods, excelling in research, information analysis, codebase navigation, and converting ideas into applications. Testing indicated stronger self-testing and verification capabilities on longer tasks.

In terms of specific benchmarks, Grok 4.6 achieved an Elo score of 1,753 on GDPVal-AA v2, a notable increase from Grok 4.5's 1,526. On CursorBench v3.2, it scored 69.9%, and on DeepSWE v1.1, it jumped to 65.9%.

Agent benchmarks also show strong performance, with Grok 4.6 reaching 57.5% on APEX-Agents, narrowly exceeding GPT-5.6 Sol Max. This focus on agentic environments is crucial as enterprise AI deployments increasingly require models to maintain state and operate tools across longer execution paths.
